I found myself unable to push through heavy mob density without the healer guardian. Used Reeza with the entanglement equipped for 2 hours straight & admired all the tiny critters putting in work, so far it's my favorite setup. Seems pretty slow until you start to upgrade movement speed back in town (durrr). The camera is too zoomed in & there needs to be an option to view the full minimap. Not because I would use it but because I don't have an option to... Visual & performance wise, the game looks & runs great but the interface could use some work. Tidy up the indicators for casting guardian's spells & integrating some various options for UI scaling/colorization. Overall good work by the Devs. I look forward to placing more time into this game.

The movement isn't very good, the animations are clunky, the enemy and map hitboxes are bad and you feel it when you try to dodge them, I found having to repeat missions to collect resources to be very weak could be improved if you add sigils or something to improve resource gain and having to wait 20 minutes in the boss phases is a long time when you compare that most missions can be completed in 5 minutes or less. The visuals are ok, the game is very easy at the beginning and for the price it's ok, but Death Must Die is far superior.

It's a very cool idea and it's a nice roguelike for people who like summoner-style builds. The game does need a bit of tweaking number/balance-wise though, as I found some guardians to be far superior to others (cloned Nipper with lifesteal is just unstoppable). One issue I had with it was when I reached the slime boss level, the game required me to survive 20 minutes before I was transported to the boss. The problem is that I had already explored the whole level within the first 7-8 minutes, meaning there was nothing to do but stand around and wait. I also reached max level at around the 15 minute mark, so after that I didn't even level up any more either. The game's progression is clearly better suited for shorter, objective based runs, and I think having these "survive for X minutes" objectives are a bad idea.

So I have put a good amount of time into the game now and I just can't recommend this game for a whole host of reasons. TLDR This is a generic vampire survivor game that shows no sign that they are gaming to move the genre or make it their own. its a Skinner box for a genre. There are better VS games out there that have a lot more interesting progression and gameplay loops. First and simply put.. it does nothing to push the genre forward. It's a very generic vampire survivor light game. it has none of the depth of some of the top VS games. Its one claim gameplay-wise is that you have pets/guardians. This has been done in a ton of VS games and honestly done better. It makes the same mistake that a lot of games do with meta-progression. It's % improvements rather than gameplay improvements. 2% increase in running, 2% in dodging..etc.. extremely boring It's EA so you would want to give them some leeway in gameplay...so..take this next with a grain of salt.. The following issues are with EA in mind. the monsters and their abilities largely suck. there are a few that are just broken OP and some that are gimmicky but if you abuse the simple gameplay you can make OP. The guardians become bloated and the reroll/black/etc system is more frustrating than interesting/gameplay changes. You are almost punished by unlocking spells/skills and after completing a mission you are forced to unlock one so you can't just skip/save your skill unlocks. The dash feels sluggish and janky. combat missions are extremely repetitive and lack any real importance to rerun other than "number go up" The story is chat gtp quality It is generic fantasy with nothing to really draw you into the world or chars The battle arenas are bland enough that after a few runs, it might as well be a blank box for how little you will care about looking at it. No synergies. The actual missions are badly designed.. take a boss battle. you will go around unlocking your guardians then run around picking up the chests.. you will have all that done before the 6-minute mark...now you will go find a wall and put your back to it. you will hit the macro that auto-ques your guardian's abilities and read up on the next seasons of solo leveling till you get close to the 20-minute mark. you will pick up the exp etc and then at the 20-minute mark fight the boss. Now you could run around that 12min killing mobs but there is no gameplay reason to do so.. you could skip macroing the abilities but there is no strategic value in queuing them up manually and finally worst of all is your punished by being efficient by having to wait till the 20min mark to fight the boss and end the zone. TLDR This is a generic vampire survivor game that shows no sign that they are gaming to move the genre or make it their own. its a Skinner box for a genre. There are better VS games out there that have a lot more interesting progression and gameplay loops.

Let's get straight to it: This game's core problem is a backwards difficulty curve, sabotaging what makes rogue-likes engaging. Why the Easy Start Fails: * Earned Progression is Key: The joy of the genre comes from overcoming challenges through learning and skill, feeling like you earned your power. * Unearned Power Feels Cheap: Starting strong removes the satisfaction loop and the thrill of a hard-won victory. * Kills Motivation: If there's no real threat, why bother learning synergies or optimizing builds? * Easy AFK = Bad Sign: Being able to coast or stand still minutes into a run highlights a lack of meaningful challenge, not player mastery. My experience confirms this: clearing early maps and bosses on the first try without dying wasn't due to skill, but a lack of resistance. The developer response seems to be that the real challenge unlocks much later – perhaps 10+ hours in. Frankly, this approach is fundamentally flawed. Gating the actual engaging gameplay behind hours of what amounts to a tedious, overly easy grind disrespects the player's time. The core loop needs to be compelling from the beginning, not treated as a chore to endure before the "real" game starts. This game desperately needs heavy balancing to introduce genuine challenge much earlier. As it stands, the progression feels unrewarding, and the promise of later difficulty isn't enough to justify the initial boredom. Until this is addressed, it's hard to recommend to anyone seeking the satisfying loop this genre typically offers. In the current state, I cannot recommend it. But then again, it’s early access and fingers crossed it will go through a lot of meaningful changes.

This game is a very capable survivors style game with a unique twist, but it has a huge problem: The first 30-60 minutes feel awful. Hitboxes are very bad, and since you're using (up to) 4 minions as your primary source of damage, who you can't directly control and who can and will die, you'll spend a number of runs feeling incredibly frustrated as your damage gets killed by what feels like very avoidable damage if only they'd stop running head-first into elite enemies, and you die to enemies whose hitboxes feel about 50% larger than they should be. If you can get past that, the game is quite good. The metaprogression adds a lot of options for increasing survivability, and once you've got a better handle on which minions you want to use together (and have more options unlocked to use), it's a lot easier to build a team that isn't going to fall over to a stiff breeze. The hitboxes never really improve, but it stops mattering as you get more defensive options yourself; the game becomes more about tanking damage than avoiding it rather quickly. One area that leaves a lot to be desired are bosses. None of the bosses are particularly difficult - in fact, I'd say the level leading up to the boss is harder in every case. The fourth (and final) boss has a glaring issue, as well: It alternates between (long) invulnerability phases where it puts out a lot of damage (which is easily avoidable by the player, but which typically demolishes your minions just due to their inability to not stand in the red circles), and brief vulnerable phases where you're expected to deal damage. The problem with this setup is that it's very common, especially on higher difficulties, for your minions to be dead when the vulnerable phase begins, and by the time they've revived, the boss is invulnerable again. Overall, the game is solid if you can get past the caveats outlined above; if you're in the mood for a survivors game that breaks the mold a bit, it's worth a buy.

You level them up with roguelike choices just as you would your character, so you can build your team all at once. You can also gear up individual summons or gear all of them at once! I LOVE this game! I came across Wildkeepers via a bundle it's currently in. I was so intrigued by the art style and when I saw it was a survivors-like I decided to try it out and I don't regret it. The gameplay is like that of Vampire Survivors except instead of one character getting all the upgrades for different weapons and spells you have five characters for each run; One 'Wildkeeper' who you choose before the run and four guardians which are selected during the run and each have their own unique attacks and abilities. There are four different areas to progress through where you acquire new Wildkeepers and guardians. There is about 6-8 hours of gameplay to finish the main progression of the game. If you want to then continue to upgrade armor and max out abilities & sigils and 100% achievements (which offer rewards in game) there is yet more incentive to replay the same areas. I do wish that there were more missions and that the story was a little more in depth but these are minor criticisms and have not prevented any enjoyment of the game. Overall, I highly recommend this game, especially if you're looking for a new survivors-like to play. I adore the art, character design and gameplay. I got it in a bundle for under four dollars but with the enjoyment I've had with Wildkeepers Rising I would've happily paid full price. I really hope to see a sequel or dlc for this game!

[b]WILDKEEPERS RISING[/b], is a very chaotic survivors-like where every mechanics clashes with one another. Every session on this game felt frustrating, whether it be the Luigi physics having you retain most momentum from moving, and having to accelerate up to speed, or the incredibly tanking mobs at higher difficulties that feel impossible to kill even with all meta upgrades, and a solid understanding on how to powerscale in these types of games. The concept and lore is actually really unique but the gameplay absolutely lets it down. Instead of you becoming the weapon, you upgrade your beasts to damage and move on their own. Which leads to many many scenarios where they ditch you do die and do their own thing in another corner of the map. The gear and meta upgrade system also feel quite unrewarding, especially for what you have to sacrifice to get the currency to level them. On top of all that, the hitboxes and visual clarity are horrendous with enemies damaging you from so far away. [b]PROS[/b]: - Unique gameplay - Lots of areas to build and minimax - Great beast diversity [b]CONS[/b]: - Extremely frustrating - Ice movememt physics - Terrible balancing - Artifical gameplay length [i]IF MY "GUARDIAN" BEASTS WOULD STOP DITCHING ME FOR ONE SECOND ESPECIALLY AS A RANGED CHARACTER THAT WOULD BE GREAT!![/i]
